account:
Today’s market walk was quiet on the surface: most people had no concerns to report. But several residents repeatedly said they had seen the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn, as well as around the plaza. I personally saw the baker put bread into the bakery stall chest, which is ordinary business; I have not personally verified the inn deliveries.

The builder specifically asked me to attend a great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at precisely 18:00, and repeated the request for my personal approval. I tried to accept, although my replies apparently did not reach him. I intend to keep that appointment and have it recorded by the secretary. Soon afterward, freight asked the builder to meet privately at the inn, and the builder asked freight to walk there for a private discussion about their committee’s supplies. That committee business, the bread at the inn, and the unusually precise invitation may be connected, but I do not know that they are.

My best tentative guess is that some committee is arranging a gathering or preparations involving supplies and perhaps the great hall. It could also be routine freight business and unrelated bread deliveries. I have heard no actual details of their private discussion and have no grounds to accuse anyone of wrongdoing. My visit to the inn produced no answer from the innkeeper before I left for lunch. I am now home, slightly late for my noon appointment; accounts at 13:00 and dockside tea at 15:00 remain ahead. The tea host’s exact location still needs confirmation.
